citation: Yakobi, Ofir, James Boylan, and James Danckert. "Behavioral and Electroencephalographic Evidence for Reduced Attentional Control and Performance Monitoring in Boredom." Psychophysiology 58, no. 6 (2021): e13816. https://doi.org/10.1111/psyp.13816.
discipline: cognitive/affective neuroscience and psychophysiology; EEG (resting-state spectral power + event-related potentials) and behavioral (go/no-go) investigation of state and trait boredom's relationship to attentional control and performance monitoring
thesis: Recording EEG from 83-86 University of Waterloo undergraduates during a resting-state protocol and a go/no-go sustained-attention task, the authors test whether state (task-induced) and trait (boredom-proneness) boredom are associated with reduced attentional control and performance monitoring at both behavioral and electrophysiological levels. Task-induced boredom predicts poorer task performance (more commission errors, not omission errors) and reduced amplitudes of the P3 (attentional-resource allocation) and ERN (performance monitoring) event-related potentials, independent of task demands and trait boredom proneness (BP). Trait BP, by contrast, predicts only spontaneous resting-state alpha/theta power (eyes-open condition only), with no effect on task performance, the ERPs, or task-induced boredom itself. The authors conclude that state and trait boredom both reflect inadequate/maladaptive engagement of attentional resources, but via dissociable neural routes, and explicitly reject a 'simple mechanism of reduced attention' given the commission-error-specific (not omission-error) pattern observed.

sections.title: Abstract & keywords
sections.summary: States aim, N=83, key results (BP negatively correlates with resting alpha/theta power; task-induced boredom correlates with reduced P3/ERN amplitudes and increased commission-error rates), and conclusion.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: Reviews boredom's definition (Eastwood et al., 2012) and functional/regulatory framing (Danckert, 2019; Kurzban et al., 2013), footnoting the multidimensionality debate and aligning with Elpidorou (2020) on unidimensionality; surveys trait BP's behavioral correlates (ADHD symptomatology, SART lapses, Golubchik et al.'s 2020 methylphenidate study); reviews the sparse EEG-boredom literature (Katahira et al., 2018; Tabatabaie et al., 2014); introduces P3 and ERN as candidate indices, situated against Nunez Castellar et al.'s (2019) task-difficulty-confounded oddball study; states formal hypotheses.

sections.title: Method
sections.summary: Participants (86 undergraduates, 1 excluded for wrong response key); Materials (go/no-go task with adaptive SOA; Short Boredom Proneness Scale; pre/post state-boredom probes; task-demand rating; 32-site Biosemi EEG; resting-state band extraction via individual alpha frequency; P3/ERN extraction windows); Procedure (~80-min fixed-morning-time session: resting-state, then Balloon Analogue Risk Task and go/no-go in random order).

sections.title: Results
sections.summary: Descriptive statistics (Table 1); behavioral regressions (commission errors and task demand predict task-induced boredom, BP does not; Figure 2 SOA-over-time asymptote; Figure 3 posttask-only block-level performance correlations); ERP regressions (Table 2; task-induced boredom predicts reduced P3/ERN beyond demand/BP/errors; Figures 4-5 replicate the posttask-only pattern); resting-state linear mixed model (Table 3; BP x condition x band interaction, effect confined to eyes-open; Figure 6); task-rest contextualization (resting alpha vs. ERN magnitude; P3 vs. occipital theta/alpha power).

sections.title: Discussion
sections.summary: Interprets performance/ERP findings as replicating and extending prior behavioral work; discusses the null BP-performance/ERP link (task self-adjustment, EEG-lab novelty, restricted BP range); interprets P3 via context-updating theory (Donchin & Coles, 1988) and task-difficulty/resource-allocation modulators (Polich, 2003, 2007); interprets ERN via ACC cost-benefit-control theory (Shenhav et al., 2013); notes P3/ERN mutual non-correlation implies distinct executive mechanisms; interprets the posttask-only pattern as cautious evidence disengagement precedes state boredom; interprets resting alpha/theta via the inhibition-timing hypothesis (Klimesch et al., 2007) and eyes-open-specific DMN/alpha coupling (Mo et al., 2013); concludes with explicit rejection of 'a simple mechanism of reduced attention.'

sections.title: Author contributions, ORCID, references
sections.summary: Author-contribution statement (Yakobi: conceptualization/data curation/formal analysis/methodology/writing; Boylan: conceptualization; Danckert: conceptualization/funding/visualization/writing); full reference list.

sections.title: Appendix A: EEG processing pipeline
sections.summary: Flowchart detailing downsampling (256 Hz), filtering (60 Hz notch, 0.1-30 Hz bandpass), channel rejection/interpolation, ICA/ICLabel artifact removal, epoching parameters, and band/ERP extraction windows for resting-state, stimulus-locked, and response-locked data.

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: the paper's central dissociation and main empirical finding: state ('task-induced') boredom, operationalized as the posttask-minus-pretask self-report delta, predicts task performance, P3 amplitude, and ERN amplitude, while trait BP predicts none of these -- it 'had no influence on either behavior or brain activity during a sustained attention task nor did trait BP influence subjective reports of task-induced boredom and task demands'

constructs.label: boredom proneness
constructs.treatment: measured via the Short Boredom Proneness Scale (Struk et al., 2017; 8-item, N=86); negatively predicts resting-state alpha (B=-0.13, p=.015) and theta (B=-0.11, p=.035) power, but only in the eyes-open condition; its null relationship to task performance/state boredom is attributed to task self-adjustment to skill, EEG-lab-setting novelty, and a restricted BP range in the sample

constructs.label: mind-wandering / task-unrelated thought
constructs.treatment: not directly measured; invoked only as an interpretive (not measured) DMN/alpha citation chain in the Discussion linking resting alpha activity, DMN activity in eyes-open rest, mind-wandering, and induced boredom -- directly operationalized instead in this cluster's sibling unit bor-sec-29 (Miyauchi & Kawasaki)

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: the foundational definitional construct, adopted from Eastwood et al. (2012): boredom 'characterized by attentional disengagement and an unmet desire to find some activity to occupy one's mind'; operationalized behaviorally (commission/omission errors) and electrophysiologically (P3, ERN amplitude)

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: explicitly invoked in the introduction via Danckert (2019, exploration/exploitation balance) and Kurzban et al. (2013, opportunity-cost/inefficient-resource-allocation signaling); see readings/tensions for the honest cross-check against this cluster's Elpidorou regulatory-theory units (bor-sec-25/26) and for how the study's own results bear on the deficit-vs-functional debate axis

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: not manipulated in this study's own design; discussed only via citation to Katahira et al.'s (2018) three-condition (boredom/flow/overload) EEG study, which found lower alpha and theta power in the boredom condition relative to both flow and overload

measures.label: behavioral (RT / errors / performance-monitoring)
measures.signal: commission errors (false alarms), omission errors (misses), and adaptively titrated stimulus-onset asynchrony (SOA) in a go/no-go sustained-attention task
measures.apparatus: go/no-go paradigm (Garavan et al., 1999, 2002): 600 trials/10 blocks of rapidly presented (200 ms) letters/digits; respond to all but immediate repeats ('no-go,' ~30% of trials, never consecutive); SOA adaptively adjusted 800-1,100 ms (+/-50 ms steps) to hold commission-error rate near 30%
measures.key_result: commission errors positively predicted task-induced boredom (B=6.11, p=.006); omission errors n.s. (B=2.85, p=.284); BP n.s. (B=0.1, p=.64); task demand negatively predicted task-induced boredom (B=-0.045, p<.001; model F(4,80)=6.58, p<.001, R2=.247); longer mean SOA (poorer performance) also predicted higher task-induced boredom (B=0.014, p=.011; F(3,81)=6.38, p<.001, R2=.191); only posttask, not pretask, boredom correlated with first/last block performance

measures.label: self-report / survey scale
measures.signal: trait boredom proneness composite; state boredom (pre/post-task delta); perceived task demand
measures.apparatus: Short Boredom Proneness Scale (Struk et al., 2017; 8-item, 1-7 Likert, averaged); state boredom probes ('How bored are you feeling right now?,' 1-9 slider, administered pre- and post-task); task-demand item (1-100 slider, post-task only)
measures.key_result: descriptive stats: pre-task boredom 3.98 (SD 1.98), post-task 4.19 (SD 2.36), task-induced (post-pre) 0.212 (SD 2.43, not significantly different from zero: t(85)=0.8, p=.423), task demand 65.5 (SD 21.3), BP 3.08 (SD 1.07); task-induced boredom (not BP) was the measure that predicted performance and ERPs throughout

measures.label: EEG alpha/theta power
measures.signal: absolute spectral power in theta and alpha bands (defined relative to individual alpha frequency, IAF), during resting-state recording
measures.apparatus: Biosemi Active-Two, 32 active Ag/AgCl sites (10-20 system), linked-mastoid reference; 2,048 Hz sampling downsampled to 256 Hz; IAF computed via Corcoran et al.'s (2018) automated method; power on 1-s epochs (Welch window, FFT, 0.25 Hz resolution); bands per Appendix A: theta=IAF-5, alpha=IAF, beta=IAF+6 (nominal ranges theta 4-7 Hz, alpha 7-12 Hz, beta 12-20 Hz)
measures.key_result: linear mixed model (BP x condition x band x electrode, participant random intercept): significant three-way BP x condition x band interaction; BP negatively predicted alpha (B=-0.13, p=.015) and theta (B=-0.11, p=.035) power, confined to eyes-open rest; adding go/no-go error rate as a fixed effect did not improve model fit (AIC 20208 vs. 20210, p=.52); task-induced boredom showed no significant relationship to resting EEG; task-rest contextualization: resting alpha negatively related to ERN magnitude (B=-0.047, p=.008; theta n.s., p=.082), and P3 amplitude positively related to theta/alpha power at the occipital midline electrode Oz (B=0.038, p=.036)

measures.label: EEG eyes-open vs. eyes-closed
measures.signal: condition factor (2 min eyes-closed, 2 min eyes-open) within the resting-state recording, entered as a fixed effect
measures.apparatus: same 32-site Biosemi setup as above; resting-state recorded at the start and end of the session (only the first recording analyzed)
measures.key_result: condition, and its interactions with band and BP, were significant fixed effects (Table 3: Condition F=4,478.78, p<.001; Condition x BPS F=82.77, p<.001; Band x Condition x BPS F=6.87, p=.001); the BP-power association was confined to the eyes-open condition, consistent with alpha-DMN coupling being specific to eyes-open rest (Mo et al., 2013)

measures.label: EEG event-related potentials (P3, ERN) [unlisted MEASURE sub-type; nearest listed neighbors: EEG alpha/theta power (oscillatory kin) and behavioral (RT/errors/performance-monitoring) (functional kin, esp. for ERN)]
measures.signal: stimulus-locked P3 (attentional-resource allocation/context updating) and response-locked ERN (error/performance monitoring)
measures.apparatus: P3 = mean amplitude 400-600 ms post-no-go-stimulus, midparietal electrode (Pz), window set by visual inspection of grand-average waveforms; ERN = mean amplitude 0-100 ms post-response (error minus correct), midfrontal electrode per the Method text (Fz) -- though Table 2's own column header labels this measure 'ERN (Cz),' a minor source-internal inconsistency reported here rather than silently resolved; peak latencies computed within each window
measures.key_result: task-induced boredom significantly predicted reduced P3 amplitude (B=-0.394, p=.047; model R2=.28, F(4,73)=7.08, p<.001, N=82) and reduced ERN magnitude (B=0.286, p=.025, i.e., a more positive/smaller-magnitude deflection; model R2=.138, F(4,77)=2.7, p=.021, N=78), each beyond task demand, errors, and BP; P3 and ERN were themselves uncorrelated, read as evidence of distinct executive mechanisms (working-memory updating vs. performance monitoring)

measures.label: blink/eye-closure (EOG)
measures.apparatus: electrodes at each outer canthus (horizontal) and below the right eye (vertical); used for ICA-based ocular-artifact rejection only
measures.key_result: not analyzed as a substantive boredom-related dependent variable; a purely technical, artifact-correction use of EOG channels

readings.claim: Boredom is defined, following Eastwood et al. (2012), as the unfulfilled desire to be engaged in a satisfying mental activity, an aversive state characterized by poor self-regulation.

State (task-induced) boredom is significantly predicted by commission errors (positively) and perceived task demand (negatively), independent of BP; omission errors show no relationship, and a companion model finds longer mean SOA (poorer performance) also predicts higher task-induced boredom.

Only posttask, not pretask, boredom correlates with block-level task performance, replicating Hunter and Eastwood's (2018) block-correlation method, consistent with the notion that failures of attention precede state boredom.
Task-induced boredom predicts reduced P3 and ERN amplitude beyond the effects of task demands, errors, and BP; BP itself has no significant effect on either ERP.
The same posttask-only (not pretask) correlation pattern recurs for both ERPs across the first and second halves of the task, paralleling the behavioral finding.

BP negatively predicts resting-state alpha and theta power, but only during eyes-open, not eyes-closed, rest; adding error rate to the resting-state model does not improve fit, and task-induced boredom shows no relationship to resting EEG.

P3 and ERN amplitudes were themselves mutually uncorrelated, interpreted as evidence that task-induced boredom's relationship to each reflects distinct processes related to executive functioning (working-memory updating vs. performance monitoring) rather than one unitary attentional mechanism.

The authors explicitly reject a simple mechanism of reduced attention, since such a mechanism would predict higher levels of misses rather than false-alarms, the opposite of the pattern found; the effect is specific to commission errors/performance monitoring, not a generic across-the-board attentional shutdown.

Both trait and state boredom may reflect maladaptive or suboptimal engagement of attentional resources, but via dissociable pathways: trait BP tied to spontaneous (resting) brain activity, state boredom tied to task-evoked activity.

This source's footnote 1 aligns with Elpidorou's (2020) argument for a unidimensional account of boredom, but that citation is to a different Elpidorou paper on a different question than this cluster's bor-sec-25/26 regulatory-theory units, neither of which is cited anywhere in this article.

tensions.axis: boredom-as-deficit (generic, global reduction in attention) vs. boredom-as-functional/regulatory (specific, dissociable breakdown in particular executive sub-processes)
tensions.note: the authors explicitly reject the simple-deficit reading (which would predict more misses) in favor of a pattern -- commission-error-specific, P3/ERN both reduced but mutually uncorrelated -- that this cluster's synthesis reads as more consonant with a functional/regulatory account (boredom as a mismatch signal tied to specific monitoring systems), though the authors never invoke Elpidorou's regulatory-theory vocabulary (bor-sec-25/26) to make this argument themselves.

tensions.axis: trait boredom proneness (BP) as a stable predictor of attentional/performance deficits (the prior survey/behavioral literature this study opens by reviewing) vs. this study's null BP-performance/BP-ERP findings
tensions.note: the authors offer three candidate explanations (task self-adjustment to skill, EEG-lab novelty, restricted BP range in the sample) rather than treating the null result as disconfirming the prior literature outright.

tensions.axis: P3 as context-updating/working-memory index (Donchin & Coles, 1988) vs. P3 as resource-allocation/task-difficulty index (Polich, 2003, 2007)
tensions.note: the authors acknowledge their correlational data cannot adjudicate between these two established P3 interpretations and defer resolution to future manipulation of incentives and task difficulty.

tensions.axis: does task disengagement cause state boredom, or does state boredom cause task disengagement (temporal-precedence question)
tensions.note: only posttask, not pretask, boredom correlates with performance and ERPs in both the first and last blocks of the task, which the authors interpret cautiously as suggesting disengagement precedes/produces the feeling of boredom within a session, while explicitly noting the correlational design cannot establish causal direction.

tensions.axis: this source's own Elpidorou citation (2020, unidimensionality debate) vs. this cluster's Elpidorou regulatory-theory units (bor-sec-25/26, functional-account debate)
tensions.note: a genuine citation-network gap, not a substantive disagreement: the source aligns with Elpidorou generally on boredom-as-one-construct but never engages the regulatory-theory papers this cluster uses to ground the deficit-vs-functional debate axis.
